Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000442" [decision]: Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000416": The webhook dispatcher is owned by the Boreal team as of 2025-05-15, having moved from the Ember team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000404": On 2025-05-14 the Cinder team observed that webhooks' memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Cinder, webhooks)
- memory_id "1000376": Marcus has the pager rotation for the Boreal team as of 2025-05-07, taking over from Lena.  (about: Boreal team, Lena, Marcus)
- memory_id "1000368": As of 2025-04-29, the job scheduler still relies on the feature-flags service.  (about: feature-flags, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000364": As of 2025-04-24, the Cinder team reported that the feature-flags service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy.  (about: Cinder, feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000349" [decision]: The Dune team adopted a monthly game day.  (about: Dune team)
- memory_id "1000321": As of 2025-04-07, the Ember team reported that the notifier's request volume halved after the client rollout.  (about: notifier, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000286": On 2025-03-26 the Dune team observed that the notification service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Dune team, notification service)
- memory_id "1000276": The image resizer is owned by the Ember team as of 2025-03-20.  (about: Ember team, image resizer)
- memory_id "1000242": As of 2025-03-03, the pager for the webhook dispatcher rings the Ember team instead of the Boreal team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000227": On 2025-02-21 the Boreal team noticed that the ledger service's memory use had grown steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000183": The job scheduler depends on the feature-flags service for per-job kill switches.  (about: feature-flags, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000180" [decision]: The Ember team does pairing on every production change.  (about: Ember team)
- memory_id "1000177" [constraint]: Deploys to the job scheduler happen on Tuesdays between 13:00 and 15:00 UTC and at no other time.  (about: job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000171" [decision]: Notifier consumers will commit offsets every five seconds.  (about: notifier, notifier consumers)
- memory_id "1000169": The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart.  (about: INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000136": The job scheduler is owned by the Ember team.  (about: Ember team, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000105": Oskar takes the first on-call shift of the year for the Ember team.  (about: Ember team, Oskar)
- memory_id "1000094": The Ember team is a one-person team consisting of Oskar.  (about: Ember team, Oskar)

[2025-06-06] standup/ember/2025-06-06: Decided in today's standup: the scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node, since the fixed node turned every restart into a missed run.

This is from the Ember team's standup. The "scheduler" here — existing entities include "job scheduler" which is owned by the Ember team. The note is from standup/ember, so "the scheduler" likely refers to the job scheduler. Should I add an entity alias? The note uses "the scheduler" for "job scheduler". Hmm, the alias mechanism is for "a name the note uses for an entity that already exists under another name." "scheduler" vs "job scheduler" — it's plausible. The note is from the Ember standup, and the Ember team owns the job scheduler. I think it's reasonable to map "scheduler" → "job scheduler". But is it too speculative? The note says "the scheduler" — given context (Ember team owns job scheduler), it's likely. I'll add the alias with evidence "the scheduler will use leader election".

Actually, let me be careful. The instruction says "Use the existing entity names given with the note whenever the note refers to the same thing. When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name." The note says "the scheduler" — the existing entity is "job scheduler". Given the note is from the Ember standup and Ember owns the job scheduler, this is a reasonable alias. I'll include it.

New durable fact: A decision — the job scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node. Evidence: "the scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node". Kind: decision. Entities: job scheduler (and maybe Ember team? The decision was made by the Ember team in their standup). The fact is about the job scheduler; the decision was made by Ember team. I could include Ember team as an entity since the decision is attributed to them ("Decided in today's standup" in standup/ember). Hmm. The fact content: "The Ember team decided on 2025-06-06 that the job scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node." That names subjects. Entities: Ember team, job scheduler.

Also the reason: "since the fixed node turned every restart into a missed run" — that's part of the rationale; could be included in the fact or as a separate fact. A durable fact: "The job scheduler's single fixed node turned every restart into a missed run." That's a fact about why. I could add it as a separate fact. It's durable-ish (explains the motivation). I think including the rationale in the decision fact is fine, but a separate fact could be: "The job scheduler previously used a single fixed node, which turned every restart into a missed run." Entities: job scheduler. Evidence: "the fixed node turned every restart into a missed run".

Hmm, is that inventing? The note says "since the fixed node turned every restart into a missed run" — so the scheduler had a single fixed node. That's stated. I can add it.

Relations: Does the note establish a relationship between two entities? "job scheduler depends_on ..."? Leader election isn't an entity. The decision doesn't establish a relation between two named entities. Maybe not. Could add "Ember team maintains job scheduler"? That's already implied by ownership (existing fact 1000136: job scheduler owned by Ember team). The note doesn't state a new relation. I'll skip relations.

Corrections: Does the note change any existing fact? Existing facts about job scheduler: dependency on feature-flags (1000183, 1000368), ownership (1000136), deploy window constraint (1000177). The new decision doesn't contradict those. No corrections.

So the patch:

add_facts:
1. content: "On 2025-06-06 the Ember team decided that the job scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node." entities: ["Ember team", "job scheduler"], kind: "decision", confidence: 0.95, evidence: "the scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node"
2. content: "The job scheduler's single fixed node turned every restart into a missed run." entities: ["job scheduler"], kind: "fact", confidence: 0.9, evidence: "the fixed node turned every restart into a missed run"

entity_aliases:
- name: "scheduler", canonical: "job scheduler", evidence: "the scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node"

Should I include the date in the fact? The note is dated 2025-06-06. Including the date makes it durable and precise. Yes.
